overview: The Göktürk Khaganate was the first empire to bear the name Türk. Founded by Bumin in 552, it stretched from Manchuria to the Black Sea, split into eastern and western halves in 583, submitted to Tang in 630 and 657, and rose again as the Second Khaganate in 682. Its stone inscriptions are the oldest Turkic writing.

items.text: The stelae of Kül Tegin (732) and Bilge Qaghan (735) in the Orkhon valley carry the oldest long texts in the Old Turkic script, the first Turkic writing.
Tengri, the sky, gave the khagan his mandate; shamans and the sacred Ötüken forest stood at the center of belief.
Taspar Qaghan patronized Buddhism and had sutras translated into Turkic, though Tengri worship remained the rule.
The khaganate held the Silk Road from China to Persia, with Sogdian merchants as its traders and scribes.
The Sogdian Maniakh, an envoy of the khagan, reached Constantinople to open a silk route around Sasanian Persia.
The name Türk first appears in history with this empire.
The Orkhon inscriptions remain the chief source for early Turkic language and history.

fall.text: An alliance of Uyghur, Basmyl and Karluk tribes overthrew the khaganate; the Uyghur Khaganate rose in its place in 744.
